issues.description: Overload signatures use a mutable-looking default in a position-significant typing fixture
issues.detail: The @overload signatures were updated to `delimiter: str | None = None`, but every other parameter in those overloads uses `= ...` (ellipsis) as the placeholder default. This is the convention the file already follows for overload stubs. Mixing literal `= None` defaults into the overloads is stylistically inconsistent with the surrounding code and could confuse static analyzers that check overload compatibility. Match the existing voice: use `= ...` in the overloads and keep `= None` only on the implementation.

issues.description: Delimiter validation only fires when the param happens to be a single string
issues.detail: The validation `if delimiter not in _PARAM_VALUE_DELIMITERS: raise ValueError(...)` is nested inside `if delimiter is not None and isinstance(items, str)`. That means calling `get_param_as_list('x', delimiter=';')` raises when the value is a single string but silently accepts the bogus delimiter when the param appeared multiple times or was already CSV-split. Same call, same bad argument, different behavior depending on the request shape. Validate the delimiter argument once at the top of the function so the contract is consistent regardless of how the value arrived.

issues.description: Two-level lookup table is doing work a one-level mapping could do
issues.detail: `_PARAM_VALUE_DELIMITERS` maps `','` to `','`, `'|'` to `'|'`, `' '` to `' '`, then aliases `'pipeDelimited'` and `'spaceDelimited'` onto the same set. The identity entries exist purely so `delimiter in _PARAM_VALUE_DELIMITERS` works as a membership check. A `frozenset` of literal delimiters plus a small alias dict (`{'pipeDelimited': '|', 'spaceDelimited': ' '}`) would say what's actually meant: there's a set of accepted characters, and two named aliases. Minor — but it's the kind of structural cleanup that pays off when someone later asks 'do we support semicolons?' and has to reason about the table.

issues.description: Empty-string and blank-value edge cases are not exercised by tests
issues.detail: The docstring explicitly calls out that `keep_blank_qs_values` does not affect the secondary split, but no test verifies what `get_param_as_list('x', delimiter=',')` returns when the value is `''`, `'a,,b'`, or `'a, b'` (whitespace around tokens). For a feature whose entire job is splitting strings, the corner cases of empty tokens and whitespace are exactly the thing the next maintainer will want a regression test for. Add a couple of explicit assertions so the documented behavior is pinned down.

review.summary: Small, scoped patch that does one thing: adds a `delimiter` kwarg to `get_param_as_list` with a documented allowlist and reasonable tests. Diff is readable, matches the surrounding style, the commit/news fragment is useful, and the splitting logic correctly defers to the multi-value path. Two real issues: the overload stubs use `= None` where the rest of the file uses `= ...`, and the delimiter validation hides inside the `isinstance(items, str)` branch so the same bad argument raises or doesn't depending on request shape — validate once up front. The lookup table is structurally over-built and the empty/blank-token cases lack tests. NEEDS-WORK on those two points, then this lands.
